subject: Crestline discovery: production readiness, latency SLOs & topology next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Crestline discovery: production readiness, latency SLOs & topology next steps

Hi Anya / Ravi —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before committing resources for a pilot. I’ve attached the SLA questionnaire you started and a very rough topology sketch for the pilot.

Key pain points you described
- Monthly reconciliation window causes traffic bursts and p95 latency spikes (observed p95 ~2–3s under batch spikes).
- Tight tail latency requirement for customer-facing workflows (search/summary flows).
- Need to keep PHI/PII on private network for certain tenant types; must run within a VPC and integrate with existing KMS.
- Cost sensitivity for high-volume inference (want a path to dedicated capacity or burst-to-spot).

Goals / acceptance criteria we discussed
- Target SLOs: p50 < 200–300 ms, p95 < 600–800 ms for 90% of queries during steady-state at expected QPS; graceful degradation (fallback model) during spikes.
- Pilot throughput: sustain 8–10 QPS with 95th percentile latency within the ranges above; scale to burst to 30 QPS for reconciliation window with degraded model fallback.
- Functional: 8k token context support (primary use), average generated tokens ~120–200, frequent short prompts for routing/intent + larger summarization tasks.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 evidence, VPC connector, customer-managed KMS, and audit log retention settings for pilot.

Initial topology suggestion (attached sketch)
- Private deployment in your VPC for PHI workloads (Redwood Private control plane, inference in your subnet).
- Dedicated GPU pool (reserved) for the steady-state baseline; autoscaling policy with capped burst to shared capacity in same region.
- Multi-variant routing: primary medium-latency/low-cost quantized model for most traffic; higher-quality model pinned for critical paths.
- KV prefix caching for repeated prompts and batching window tuned to 50–100 ms to balance latency vs throughput.

Data & artifacts we need from you to scope the pilot
1) A 48–72 hour traffic sample (timestamps, payload size, typical prompt lengths).
2) 20–30 representative prompts + expected outputs (we'll run quality checks across candidate models).
3) Security contacts & any vendor questionnaire fields you want completed (I attached the partial questionnaire).

Proposed next steps / timeline
- You: share traffic sample and sample prompts by EOD Monday (Oct 26).
- Us: review artifacts and propose pilot configuration and cost estimate by Oct 29.
- Schedule a 60-min ops/deep-dive with your infra and security team the week of Nov 1 to finalize VPC/KMS details.

Action owners
- Jordan: pilot config draft & cost estimate (deliver Oct 29).
- Ben: commercial template & rough T-shirt pricing for dedicated vs hosted (in parallel).
- Marissa: SLO verification test plan and KV/cache tuning suggestions.

If that all looks right, I’ll put the Oct 29 deliverable and the Nov 2 ops-deep-dive on our calendars and loop in the engineers.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Crestline discovery: production readiness, latency SLOs & topology next steps

Thanks Jordan — this summary is helpful and accurate. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Security/compliance: we will need the SOC 2 type II report and a short data flow diagram showing where logs and inference data will reside during the pilot. KMS must be customer-managed.
2) Pilot sizing: the reconciliation window is predictable — it’s a daily 30-minute batch, peak QPS ~28 sustained for 30 minutes, baseline QPS ~6 for the remainder of the day. We can mock up traffic if the sample window isn’t available immediately.
3) Model fidelity: for our summarization flows we need edge-case fidelity (long medical notes). If a quantized 30B model meets p95 we’d prefer it for cost. If not, we’ll need a fallback plan to a higher-capacity instance for those flows.

Action items from our side
- Ravi (cc’d) will package a 72-hour trace and generate the 20 sample prompts by Oct 26.
- Security: I’ll share our vendor questionnaire and SSO/contact for the Nov ops call.

We’re comfortable with the proposed pilot timeline. Please include a short runbook for how Redwood would handle an incident during the reconciliation window (alerts, failover steps, communication path).

Folks — short internal follow-up after Anya’s note. I set the deadlines in the recap above and noted the pilot expectations. Below are the immediate internal asks so we can deliver on Oct 29 and be ready for the Nov 2 ops call.

Immediate internal tasks
- Marissa: SLO verification plan + KV/cache tuning experiment design. Deliverable: one-page test plan and expected metrics (p50/p95/p99) by Oct 28.
- Ben: draft POC commercial runbook + pricing options (hosted burst vs dedicated 12mo) by Oct 29. Include the two-week evaluation credit and onboarding fee scenarios.
- Jordan: pilot config draft (node sizing, model candidates, fallback routing policy) & incident runbook (how we detect and respond to reconciliation spikes) by Oct 29. I’ll also prepare the short runbook Anya requested for incident handling.

Notes for the pilot config:
- Candidate models to evaluate: quantized 30B family (low-cost baseline), 70B high-fidelity candidate for edge-case fallback.
- Autoscaling policy: baseline min capacity to cover 8 QPS with headroom; burst policy to allow immediate +2x capacity by routing to shared pool but with automatic model-fallback after 60s if queue grows.

I’ll create the calendar invites for the Nov 2 ops call (60 min) and the Oct 29 checkpoint (internal review).

Thanks —
